research_contract.question: How can project owners retain the right intent and evidence while avoiding repeated full-context reconstruction?
source_scopes: Public project entry and recovery contracts
Owner-approved comparisons of targeted source windows and complete-context baselines
research_contract.decision_to_change: Choose entry points, source retrieval, handoff content and compaction practices that preserve binding intent at a lower total reconstruction cost.
success_criteria: Recover the correct source, current constraint, owner and next action in a cold read.
Measure lost nuance, reconstruction effort and resulting rework alongside input size.
falsifiers: Reduced context omits a binding requirement or source correction that the comparison baseline recovers.
Retrieval and repair costs erase the reduction in repeated reading.
evidence_gaps: A smaller context or intact content hash does not establish authorship, intent preservation or improved outcomes.
watch_triggers: New owner-approved outcome or counterexample changes the decision evidence.
The relevant source, operating constraint or acceptance boundary materially changes.
research_contract.answer_shape: A bounded comparison of entry, retrieval and recovery approaches with missed-intent cases, recovery cost and conditions for use.
research_contract.refresh_policy: Review when relevant owner evidence or decision conditions change; registration starts no collector, benchmark, scheduler or new execution lane.
research_contract.state_note: Library-authored proposed criteria and counterevidence, not an evaluated method or accepted answer. This metadata does not establish measured gains, commercial commitments or authorization for new execution.
